# ankra_alert_rule (Resource)

An alert definition (`ankra alerts rules`): the rules Ankra evaluates against the organisation's clusters, and the alert destinations it notifies when one fires. Setting `enabled = false` mutes the alert: its history is kept, an open incident is settled, and nothing new fires until it is enabled again. The platform reports how many rules an alert holds but not the rules themselves, so `rules` is kept as configured; a rule count that no longer matches plans the rules again, and every change to `rules` replaces the alert's whole rule set. An imported alert adopts the configured `rules` on the first apply. Destroy deletes the alert and its rules. Needs an Ankra platform from 2026-11-08 or later.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ankra_alert_rule" "disk_pressure" {
  name              = "node-disk-pressure"
  description       = "Nodes running out of disk"
  destination_names = [ankra_alert_destination.ops.name]

  rules = [{
    name          = "disk pressure"
    resource_type = "node"
    all_clusters  = true
    severity      = "critical"
    conditions = [{
      condition_type     = "status"
      condition_operator = "equals"
      condition_value    = "DiskPressure"
    }]
  }]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Alert name, unique in the organisation.
- `rules` (Attributes List) The rules of the alert, at least one. The alert fires when any rule's conditions hold. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free-text description.
- `destination_names` (Set of String) Names of the alert destinations (`ankra_alert_destination`) notified when the alert fires. A name that matches no destination fails the apply.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the alert is evaluated and notifies. Defaults to `true`; `false` mutes it.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identifier of the alert.
- `rule_count` (Number) How many rules the platform stores for the alert.
- `severity` (String) The highest severity among the alert's rules.
- `state` (String) Lifecycle state of the alert on the platform.

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Required:

- `conditions` (Attributes List) Conditions of the rule, joined by each condition's `logical_operator`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--conditions))
- `name` (String) Rule name.
- `resource_type` (String) Kind of resource the rule evaluates, such as `cluster`, `node`, `pod` or `addon`.

Optional:

- `all_clusters` (Boolean) Whether the rule applies to every cluster of the organisation, including clusters added later.
- `cluster_ids` (Set of String) Clusters the rule applies to.
- `cluster_resource_types` (Set of String) Kubernetes resource kinds a cluster-wide rule evaluates.
- `cooldown_minutes` (Number) Minutes after a firing before the rule may fire again. The platform default is 5.
- `description` (String) Free-text description of the rule.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule is evaluated. The platform default is `true`.
- `environments` (Set of String) Cluster environments the rule applies to, such as `production`.
- `min_failure_duration_minutes` (Number) Minutes the conditions must hold before the rule fires, 0 to 1440; unset uses the evaluator's default.
- `resource_id` (String) Identifier of the one resource the rule evaluates; unset evaluates every resource of `resource_type` the rule's clusters hold.
- `resource_name_pattern` (String) Pattern a resource's name must match for the rule to evaluate it.
- `severity` (String) `critical`, `warning` or `info`. The platform default is `warning`.

<a id="nestedatt--rules--conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.conditions`

Required:

- `condition_operator` (String) How the value is compared, such as `equals` or `greater_than`.
- `condition_type` (String) What the condition reads, such as `status` or a metric.
- `condition_value` (String) The value compared against, such as `DiskPressure`.

Optional:

- `logical_operator` (String) `AND` or `OR`, joining the condition to the others. The platform default is `AND`.
- `threshold_value` (Number) Numeric threshold of a metric condition.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Imported by alert id. The first apply writes the configured rules.
terraform import ankra_alert_rule.disk_pressure 4c2a9e1f-2222-4333-8444-955556666777
```
